sentences.english_text: Drippy suddenly heard voices, and he pressed down against the table to stay out of sight.
Four men came into the room.
They looked enormous to Drippy.
He studied their faces, and he did not like what he saw.
They had mean eyes and mean faces and harsh voices.
One of the men had a beard.
He said, Everything is all set.
We're going to rob the bank tonight.
They were going to rob a bank.
That was against the law.
Drippy wished that there was some way he could warn the police of what was going to happen.
But of course, there was no way.
One of the men said, What will we do with that tear in the box?
The bearded man answered, It's worth a fortune to us.
We'll keep it here until after the bank job, and then we'll send a ransom note.
Drippy was not sure what a ransom note was, but it did not sound good.
He watched as the man walked over to the iron box.
Drippy held his breath.
If the man looked inside and saw that the tear was not there, they would begin a search, and they would find him.
And Heaven only knew what they would do to him after they found him.
But Drippy was in luck.
The man closed the box without looking inside and locked it.
No one knew that Drippy had escaped.
I'm safe.
As soon as they leave, I'll just slip out of here and find Mr. Wind or Mr. Pigeon or Mr. Snail, and they will help me escape.
But it was not to be.
The man with the beard pulled out a map from his pocket and laid it across the table, right next to where Drippy was hiding.
Here's the plan of the bank.
We cut off the alarm, go in through the back door, and go down to the vault where all our money is.
All the men leaned over to study the map.
One of them said, There shouldn't be any problem.
Have you got your guns?
The four men pulled out guns that looked enormous to Drippy.
I hope they're not planning to use them.
Drippy thought.
He had seen what guns could do.
